english.title: Wildlife - fail to assist inspector examining bird / animal for section 14 offence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed, without reasonable excuse, to give any assistance when reasonably required, to an authorised wildlife inspector, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME..), to ascertain if any offence under section 14 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 had been committed against a specimen, namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMAL/BIRD..), which was in your possession or control
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 19ZA(7)(b), 21(4A) and (4B) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 19ZA(6) imposes a duty to assist a wildlife inspector entering premises to examine a bird or other animal
(ii) offence wording H3837 concerns the failure to assist a wildlife inspector examining a bird or animal to ascertain whether a (less serious) offence under Section 6, 7, 9(5) or 13(2) has occurred.
(iii) As inserted by paragraph 8 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
